newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy train derailment probe focuses on speed.
newsitem.headline: Italy train derailment probe focuses on speed.

text.p: Italian authorities on Monday focused on speed as a possible cause for the derailment of an express in northern Italy that killed eight people.

The Milan-to-Rome train shot off the tracks as it rounded a curve a short distance before the Piacenza station on Sunday afternoon. The train's two engineers were among the victims and another 30 passengers were injured.

Police, firefighters and railroad employees worked through the night to clear debris from the tracks. A public prosecutor and Italy's Ferrovie dello Stato railroad opened separate investigations into the cause of the accident.
Delays of up to three hours in rail services between northern and southern Italy were reported on Monday as trains continued to be diverted around Piacenza.
Investigators said the train's "black box", which was recovered on Sunday, would be studied to determine how fast it had been travelling when it left the track.
Rail officials have said regulations required trains not to exceed 105 km per hour (60 mph) around the Piacenza curve.
The COMU union representing Italy's train engineers issued a statement late on Sunday in which it said human error was not to blame and blasted the railroad for "lax safety checks".
The union also announced that it would stage a strike from noon to 2 p.m. (1100-1300 GMT) on Thursday to draw attention to its claims of safety problems.
The railroad's managing director Giancarlo Cimolo said Italy's trains were "the safest in Europe".
